title: Massless Islands in Wedge Holography
summary: Entanglement islands are most easily realized in doubly holographic models with massive gravitons or non-gravitating baths. In wedge holography, however, Neumann boundary conditions on both branes give a normalizable massless graviton, while the island saddle of the purely geometric Ryu--Takayanagi (RT) problem collapses to the horizon. Negative Dvali--Gabadadze--Porrati (DGP) terms can restore nontrivial islands by modifying the endpoint condition, but this branch contains a massive ghost.
